Construct a portable conversation history

Source: R/history.R
conversation_history.Rd

Converts native ellmer user and assistant turns into a versioned envelope containing only allowlisted conversation data. Tool requests and results are retained as data; they are never executed. System turns and unsupported or nonportable content fail explicitly.

Usage

conversation_history(turns = list())

Arguments

turns

An unnamed list of ellmer UserTurn and AssistantTurn objects. The empty list constructs an empty history.

Value

An object with class dsprrr_history. This constructor creates a version-1 empty or ReAct history. RLM execution returns version-2 history containing observed invocation exchanges in result metadata.

Details

Supported content includes text, JSON, thinking with JSON-safe extra data, inline and remote images, PDFs, tool requests, and tool results. Runtime tool objects are omitted. A tool result may contain JSON-safe data or an ordered list of allowlisted content. Condition errors are retained as their message; runtime condition and call objects are dropped. Uploaded content and arbitrary R objects are rejected. Tool request IDs must be unique and every request must have one matching result before the history is accepted. Histories are limited to 64 data nesting levels, 12 MiB of data, 16 MiB of JSON, 10,000 turns, and 100,000 tagged values.

Histories are copied into a tagged data representation. They do not retain ellmer Chat objects, functions, environments, external pointers, credentials attached to runtime tools, or usage, cost, or duration metadata. Conversation text, reasoning, media, and tool data may still be sensitive; protect saved history files accordingly.

RLM histories instead store visible task previews, inert code and observed output text, plus complete typed final outputs. They do not restore variables or interpreter state. ReAct turns and RLM exchanges cannot be mixed.

Saved JSON is limited to 16 MiB; retained string and media data are limited to 12 MiB. Histories also have limits on turns, nesting depth, and values. RLM histories additionally retain at most 100 exchanges and 1,000 observed steps, with a canonical rendered context limit of 128 KiB. Oversized histories fail explicitly rather than silently truncating evidence.

Examples

turns <- list(
  ellmer::UserTurn(list(ellmer::ContentText("What is 2 + 2?"))),
  ellmer::AssistantTurn(list(ellmer::ContentText("4")))
)
history <- conversation_history(turns)
identical(length(history_turns(history)), 2L)
#> [1] TRUE
